extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants, peer reviewers, Scientific Review Officers, and NIH extramural staff
extracted.subtask_short: NIH peer review of research grants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the NIH dual-level peer review process for research grant and cooperative agreement applications, including reviewer roles, scored review criteria, additional considerations, scoring procedures, appeals, and second-level Advisory Council review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core values of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review should be fair, equitable, timely, and free of bias; these core values form the foundation for the laws, regulations, and policies that govern the NIH peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH dual peer review system is mandated by statute (section 492 of the Public Health Service Act) and federal regulations; policy is intended to promote review consistent with these core values.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOA-specified review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) specifies all of the review criteria and considerations that will be used in the evaluation of applications submitted for that FOA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for Applications (RFAs) and certain Program Announcements may include additional review criteria and considerations; other funding opportunity types (e.g., construction, fellowships) may use different criteria. Unless the FOA specifies otherwise, standard NIH review procedures apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Review Officer (SRO) responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: SRO is responsible for ensuring each application receives an objective and fair initial peer review and that applicable laws, regulations, and policies are followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SROs analyze content and check completeness, document and manage conflicts of interest, recruit qualified reviewers, assign applications to reviewers, attend and oversee administrative/regulatory aspects of meetings, and prepare summary statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer recruitment considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should be recruited based on scientific and technical qualifications and other considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recruitment considerations include authority in their scientific field; dedication to high quality, fair, and objective reviews; ability to work collegially in a group setting; experience in research grant review; and balanced representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: SRG Chair role
rubrics_metrics.description: Chair serves as moderator of the discussion of scientific and technical merit and also serves as a peer reviewer for the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair manages the discussion to ensure fair consideration of applications and adherence to procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer duties and conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must declare conflicts of interest, maintain confidentiality, prepare written critiques, assign numerical scores to each scored review criterion, and make recommendations on merit and applicable protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers receive applications ~6 weeks prior, must follow NIH guidance on COI and confidentiality, provide written critiques as directed by the SRO, assign criterion scores, recommend protections for human subjects, inclusion, vertebrate animals, and advise on budget appropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant conduct during peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must maintain the integrity of the peer review process by not contacting reviewers, not sending information directly to a reviewer, and not accessing information related to the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are consequences for violating confidentiality or attempting to influence review outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers provide an overall impact score reflecting their assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall impact is given in consideration of the scored review criteria and any additional review criteria applicable to the project; reviewers provide a preliminary overall impact score before meetings and final impact scores after discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance (scored criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance is one of the scored review criteria used to evaluate research grant applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significance is considered by reviewers when determining scientific and technical merit and in providing an overall impact score; reviewers assign a numerical score for this criterion (1–9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s) (scored criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigator(s) is one of the scored review criteria used to evaluate research grant applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate the qualifications, capabilities, and appropriateness of the investigators and assign a numerical score for this criterion (1–9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation (scored criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovation is one of the scored review criteria used to evaluate research grant applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess whether the project uses novel concepts, approaches or methods and assign a numerical score for this criterion (1–9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach (scored criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach is one of the scored review criteria used to evaluate research grant applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate the rigor, feasibility, and appropriateness of the study design and methods and assign a numerical score for this criterion (1–9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment (scored criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Environment is one of the scored review criteria used to evaluate research grant applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess institutional support, resources, and environment's contribution to success and assign a numerical score for this criterion (1–9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review criteria (evaluated but not separately scored)
rubrics_metrics.description: Items evaluated as applicable while determining scientific and technical merit and providing an overall impact score, but not given separate criterion scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: Study Timeline (clinical trials), Protections for Human Subjects, Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Children, Vertebrate Animals, Biohazards, Resubmission, Renewal, Revision. Reviewers consider these items in their overall impact assessment where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review considerations (not scored and not for overall impact)
rubrics_metrics.description: Items reviewers should consider as applicable, but should not give scores for and should not consider in providing an overall impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: Applications from Foreign Organizations; Select Agent; Resource Sharing Plans; Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources; Budget and Period Support. These factors may still inform programmatic or administrative decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH scoring scale and calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH uses a 9-point rating scale (1 = exceptional; 9 = poor) for all applications; the same scale is used for overall impact and criterion scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before the meeting, assigned reviewers give separate scores for each scored criterion and a preliminary overall impact score. For discussed applications, final impact scores are provided by eligible committee members, and the mean of final impact scores is multiplied by 10 to yield a final overall impact score reported on the summary statement (range 10–90). Applications not discussed are designated ND (may be reported as ++).

rubrics_metrics.name: Not Recommended for Further Consideration (NRFC) grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be designated NRFC by the SRG if it lacks significant and substantial merit or presents serious ethical problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific NRFC reasons include lack of significant/substantial merit; serious ethical problems in protection of human subjects; or serious ethical problems in use of vertebrate animals, biohazards, and/or select agents. NRFC apps do not proceed to second-level review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary statement content and ND designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary statements report scores and written comments; applications not discussed receive ND designation but the applicant and NIH staff still see the written comments and criterion scores from assigned reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ND may be reported as ++ on the face page; summary statements identify the base used to determine percentiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentile ranking explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: A percentile approximates the percentage of applications that received a better overall impact score from the study section during the past year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Percentiles are reported as whole numbers; only a subset of applications receive percentiles; ad hoc study sections may use a different base; the summary statement will identify the base used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals grounds for peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators may appeal initial review results if they believe the review process was flawed for specific reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable appeal reasons include bias of a reviewer, conflict of interest, absence of appropriate expertise, or factual errors by one or more reviewers that could have substantially altered the review outcome. The appeal policy does not apply to technical evaluation appeals for R&D contract projects, NIH funding decisions, or MERIT award extension decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-level (Advisory Council/Board) review considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory Councils/Boards consider program staff analyses, overall impact scores, percentile rankings (if applicable), summary statements, and the Institute/Center's priorities when reviewing applications at the second level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program staff provide a grant-funding plan to Council; Council members have access to applications and summary statements pending funding; Council may conduct Special Council Review for investigators receiving $1M+ direct costs to consider additional funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation and final funding decision process
rubrics_metrics.description: Only applications recommended for approval by both the SRG and the Advisory Council may be recommended for funding; final funding decisions are made by the Institute/Center Directors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program staff consider SRG scores, percentiles, summary statements, and IC priorities when advising the Director; if awarded, applicants work with program officials and grants management officers on award administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer access and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Assigned reviewers receive access to grant applications approximately six weeks prior to the peer review meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This timing supports preparation of written critiques and scoring in accordance with review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget review by reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may make recommendations concerning the appropriateness of budget requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Budget Information for Reviewers guidance; budget and period support are listed among additional review considerations and should not be used in overall impact scoring.
